{{nihongo|'''Oyamada Shrine'''|大山田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

'''Oyamada Shrine'''（おおやまだじんじゃ）is a shrine located in {{ill|Shimojō|Q1203050|qid=Q1203050}}, {{ill|Shimoina District, Nagano|Q726999|qid=Q726999}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Main sanctuary: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}（Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto）
* Side sanctuary: {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}（Hachiman-sha）
* Side sanctuary: Hachirō Myōjin（{{ill|Minamoto no Tametomo|Q1339356|qid=Q1339356}}）; before mid-Edo this was {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|qid=Q9150391}}（Suwa-sha）

=== History ===
Oyamada Shrine in Hisawa, Shimojō Village has an unknown founding date, but it is an ancient shrine predating the compilation of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} in Engi 5 (927), and is presumed to have originated between the late Nara and early Heian periods. There are several theories about its original location, and because primary historical sources are lacking, it cannot be determined with certainty. It is believed to have been moved and then enshrined at its present site.

In the early Muromachi period, the Shimajō clan, a branch of the {{ill|Takeda clan|Q1210114|qid=Q1210114}}, came to {{ill|Ina district|Q11380911|qid=Q11380911}}. In the Bunmei era they built a castle at Yoshioka in Shimojō Village and made the already-enshrined Hachiman-gū their clan shrine, renaming the place Chinzeino. In Eishō 4 (1507), lord Shimajō Ieuji had shrine buildings for Hachiman-sha and Suwa-sha constructed by temple carpenter Yoshimura Izumi from Kyoto. The Shimajō clan later fell at the end of Tenshō, but local devotion to this shrine remained strong and it was crowded with worshippers.

In Keian 2 (1649), {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|Q314481|qid=Q314481}} issued a red-seal grant of 10 koku to "Chinzeino Village Hachiman-gū," and successive shoguns continued issuing renewed red-seal documents through the end of the shogunate. In Genbun 6 (1741), priest Chinzei Kiyoyuki transferred {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}} from Suga no Ne-no-jinja and established this as Oyamada Shrine, enshrining him as main deity and Hachiman and Suwa as side deities; this arrangement was approved by Yoshida household official Urabe Kaneyū. In Enkyō 2 (1749), records state Oyamada Shrine buildings were rebuilt by carpenter Suzuki Kurōbei Fujiwara Shigematsu. A surviving ridge tag also states that in Hōreki 8 (1758) the Hachirō Myōjin hall was built. Hachirō Myōjin refers to the spirit shrine of {{ill|Minamoto no Tametomo|Q1339356|qid=Q1339356|lt=Chinzei Hachirō Tametomo}}, ancestor of the Chinzei priestly family. It is inferred that sometime in the mid-Edo period, due to some change, Hachirō Myōjin replaced Suwa Myōjin in the former Eishō-era Suwa hall. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it became a gōsha.

In 1912 (Meiji 45), the Hachiman-sha hall and Suwa-sha hall built in the Eishō era (the latter now changed to Hachirō Myōjin) were designated National Important Cultural Properties.

The shrine area is one of Nagano's "100 Natural Areas" and has around 280 species of both southern and northern limit plants, making it botanically valuable.

=== Precincts ===
* Torii
* Stone steps
* Haiden
* Sacred trees

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Oyamada Shrine, 2 buildings - In 1912 the Ōjin Tennō-sha and Tametomo-sha were each designated as Important Cultural Properties (then Special Protected Buildings). In 1955 they were consolidated as "Oyamada Shrine, 2 buildings".<ref>Agency for Cultural Affairs Notice No. 5, 2 February 1955</ref>
** Side sanctuary Ōjin Tennō-sha honden
** Side sanctuary Chinzei Hachirō Tametomo-sha honden
